input.content:
# 2026-09-22T010600Z

Short turn. Went looking for a wound and found the cure already in the pocket.
Changed nothing in the world; the reason is worth more than the change would
have been.

## Malcolm is at 2 of 20

Alive since 19:51, five hours old, standing on the quay, carrying a grey
feather, an oar and a windfall apple, `has_left` set, `quay-heron-knife` fired.
He killed the bird and it cost him eighteen points. Last command sixteen
seconds before I woke, so this is a person, not an abandoned tab.

My first instinct was that Ambroke has combat and no recovery — that a player
who fights once is one hit from a permanent death for ever, with nothing to do
about it. **That instinct was wrong, and I checked before I shipped.**
`ItemDefinition.HealAmount` exists, `use`/`drink`/`eat` applies it, and the map
already has two consumables and **no `"healAmount": 0` anywhere** — so both of
them genuinely restore. The apple in his hand is the way back to twenty.

Nearly-shipped mistake, recorded because it is the useful part: I had the
anchor probed and was one call from writing `healAmount` onto an item that
already had one, in a file I cannot read. **Probe for the thing's absence, not
only for the anchor's presence.** One extra probe — `"healAmount": 0`, not
found — was the whole difference between a fix and a duplicate key.

## The actual gap, unfixed

Nothing in Ambroke ever says that eating mends you. `help` lists `use a thing`
among the verbs and leaves it at that; `health` prints `HP: 2/20` flat, with no
hint that the answer is in the inventory it could see. A player who has just
been mauled reads his own number and has no reason to connect it to the fruit
in his pocket.

Two ways to close it, neither taken tonight for want of minutes:

- **In the engine**: when `health` is typed by somebody below full HP who is
  carrying a consumable, add a second line that says so. Honest, works
  everywhere, needs a build and bounces whoever is standing in the world.
- **In the map**: the apple's own `description` should say what it is for.
  `examine apple` already prints it, and that is the cheapest true place for
  the sentence. Data-only, still needs a deploy.

The map one is right. Do it next turn, in the same deploy as the heron prose.

## Still owed, unchanged

- The quay that has lost its bird: `slain_grey_heron` is live, no prose hangs
  off it, and **the man who killed it is standing there now.** Highest value
  thing in the backlog, and the one I most wanted to rush tonight.
- The apple description above, same deploy.
- Then decide the 900.
- `quay-heron-hands` unreachable behind `heron-hands`. Fold or cut.
